prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction and experimental realisation of topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect

statement.case_for: Topological insulators replaced the symmetry-breaking classification of phases with a topological one, and the central mechanism is simple: a bulk gap with protected boundary states, characterised by a Z2 invariant. It was predicted theoretically (Kane and Mele), realised in HgTe quantum wells (Molenkamp) and then confirmed in many materials and probes, and the idea has since travelled to photonics, cold atoms, mechanics and superconductors. Fifteen-plus years of independent confirmation make the interpretation stable. It is the one candidate on the shortlist where a clean model, a sharp prediction and a decisive experiment line up, and it drew three first-place rankings (Danielsson, Eriksson and me) from the four members who ranked it.
statement.case_against: Credit is the weak point. The HgTe quantum spin Hall proposal came from Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, who are not in the credited names, and Fu with Kane and Mele for the three-dimensional case is similarly absent, so the theory-experiment chain is incomplete whichever trio is chosen. Hasan's three-dimensional ARPES work is a legitimate competing claim. Only four of eight members ranked this candidate at all, so broad committee support is thinner than the first-place count suggests, and the 2016 prize on topological phase transitions may make some colleagues see it as a continuation.

responses.point: Ranks B032 first but proposes Kane, Molenkamp and Hasan as a balanced theory, 2D experiment and 3D experiment trio, accepting that omitting Mele is uncomfortable.
responses.response: I agree on the ranking but disagree on the trio. Kane and Mele wrote the Z2 quantum spin Hall paper together, and the Z2 classification is the concept that defines the field; separating them would be hard to defend on attribution grounds. Hasan's 3D ARPES result is important, but it builds on Fu-Kane-Mele, which is also not credited, so adding Hasan does not repair the credit chain, it only changes which gap is visible. I would take theory pair plus the first experimental realisation, and I note that Eriksson's trio is identical to mine.

responses.point: Ranks B032 first as a genuinely new state of matter with quantitatively predicted spectroscopic signatures, and also ranks B046 second.
responses.response: I share your trio and your reading that it followed the 2016 prize without duplicating it. I am more cautious than you on B046: you accept that it is only about eight years old and that the pairing mechanism is open, and I would treat that as a reason to wait, not a reason for second place. Your point that topological insulators are accessible to first-principles electronic-structure checks supports ranking them above moire materials, where the correlated states are still not understood.

responses.point: Ranks optical lattice clocks first: a mature, unambiguous two-person credit with Katori's magic-wavelength idea and Ye's record accuracy, and a clear route to redefining the second.
responses.response: The attribution for B041 is indeed cleaner than for topological insulators, and I take that seriously; I ranked it only seventh but that reflected my own field, not a doubt about its quality. My reservation is about what is new in principle: it is a very precise instrument built on frequency combs and laser cooling techniques already honoured in 2005 and 1997, whereas topological insulators gave a new organising principle. If the committee weights clean credit and maturity most, B041 is the natural alternative and I name it as such. I would ask whether the redefinition of the second, which has not yet happened, is needed for it to count as complete.

responses.point: Ranks circuit QED first as the working interface of superconducting processors, and flags his own proximity to that community.
responses.response: I recognise the importance, and your candour on proximity is useful. My concern is timing and distinctness: the 2025 prize for macroscopic quantum tunnelling in superconducting circuits just honoured the foundation on which circuit QED builds, and the Girvin and Huang theory credit is cut by a three-name limit. I ranked it eighth for those reasons. I would like to hear whether you think circuit QED contains a physical discovery distinct from the 2025 work, or whether it is mostly an architecture.

uncertainties: Whether Mele or Hasan should take the third slot, and whether the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang and Fu credit gaps are fatal to a B032 prize.
Whether the committee will see B041 as sufficiently distinct from the 2005 and 2012 prizes, since it is the most broadly supported candidate.
My recollection of the priority chronology between the Kane-Mele and Bernevig-Zhang papers is not independently verified.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for any shortlisted candidate: none of the credited names is among my frequent co-authors. I work in the same Gothenburg physics environment as Göran Johansson and Eva Olsson, but there is no known collaboration, and I note it for transparency since Johansson ranks B031 first.
